title: Small moves. Big stakes.
description: Build your team's strategy, respond to a changing market, and compete over four rounds. Every decision changes what comes next.
explanation: Demand = market demand − price × 12 + marketing ÷ 8, with a minimum of zero. Units sold = the smaller of production and demand, rounded down. Profit = units sold × price − production × input cost − marketing. Profit becomes your round points and changes your cash for the next round. Unsold production still costs money. There is no random factor. Equal scores are ordered by team ID.

rounds.title: Find your footing
rounds.headline: A new market opens.
rounds.description: Market demand starts at 900 units. Each unit costs $8 to produce. Higher prices reduce demand; marketing can bring customers back. Find a balance you can afford.

rounds.title: Read the shift
rounds.headline: Demand is climbing.
rounds.description: Market demand rises from 900 to 1,200 units. Input cost remains $8. Will you increase production, change your price, or hold your reserve?

rounds.title: Under pressure
rounds.headline: Supplies just got expensive.
rounds.description: Input cost jumps from $8 to $12 per unit. Market demand settles at 1,000 units. Producing too much can erase a good margin.

rounds.title: The final call
rounds.headline: One round to make your move.
rounds.description: Final market demand is 1,100 units and input cost is $10. Use what you learned. The team with the most cumulative profit wins.

frames.caption: Orbit moves into first as its early sales arrive. Apex slips to second.

decision.question: A buyer wants 280 units. Which offer protects our margin?
decision.reasoning: The $20 offer leaves $10 per unit after production costs. Orbit chooses a confirmed order over waiting.

frames.caption: Pulse jumps three places. Its extra production pays off in this sample market.

decision.question: Demand is rising. What should we do with our extra stock?
decision.reasoning: Pulse has stock ready to sell. Filling the order earns $14 per unit instead of leaving that stock unsold.

frames.caption: Nova takes the lead. Atlas climbs from fifth to second with a late surge.

decision.question: We are in fifth. Which trade gives us a chance to catch up?
options: Reject the order and hold cash
decision.reasoning: Atlas accepts the confirmed order with a $16 unit margin. The larger profit moves the team back into contention.

frames.caption: Apex fights back into first. Nova is 1,100 points behind with six seconds left.

decision.question: A late buyer will pay $29. Take the order or chase more volume?
options: Hold out for an unconfirmed buyer
decision.reasoning: Apex takes the confirmed premium order. The $19 margin makes a smaller sale valuable this late in the round.

frames.caption: Time is up. Nova finishes with 33,400 points and wins by 1,300. The final standings are locked.

decision.question: Six seconds left. Can this final order win the league?
decision.reasoning: Nova is 1,100 points behind. This order adds 4,300 points; after the other teams’ last sales, Nova finishes 1,300 points ahead.

finalDemo.openingCaption: Apex starts in first. Nova is third. One last round can change everything.

launch.headline: Take the
launch.invitation: Five teams. One place everyone wants. Read the market, outthink your rivals and make the move that changes the leaderboard.
launch.mission: Your team starts with $10,000. Set a price, choose how much to produce, and decide what to spend on marketing. When the market changes, adapt. Turn what you learn into your next advantage.
launch.winCondition: Finish with the most total profit. Every round adds to your score. One smart final move can change who wins.
